html:
Slack

The slack skill performs live workspace operations. Enable Slack in the existing Skills capability policy. Slack owns messages, conversations and files. The skill has no workspace mirror, index, crawler, background listener or helper model. The main Agent interprets requests and summarizes the bounded results.

Configure and connect

In Parameter Store, select Slack OAuth App, fill in the app's client ID and private client secret, select scopes, and save as (for example) slack_app. The template requests no scopes by default: explicitly choose the minimum needed. Register the exact callback with your Slack app:

https://your-controller/api/agent/slack/oauth/callback

Slack requires HTTPS for registered callbacks. Desktop installations therefore need a trusted HTTPS route to their existing controller. An HTTP loopback callback is not offered. The controller's request origin must match the registered URL. See Slack's installation guidance.

Choose flow: "user" for personal channel/DM access and search. Set requested_user_scopes, leaving requested_bot_scopes empty. This uses oauth/v2_user/authorize and oauth.v2.user.access, including S256 PKCE. Choose flow: "workspace" for a bot, set requested_bot_scopes, and add user scopes only if needed. That flow uses oauth/v2/authorize and oauth.v2.access; it does not assume that endpoint supports PKCE. Both flows use expiring single-use state, private launch tickets and confidential client authentication. User-only endpoint, workspace endpoint.

Ask the Agent to connect using the exact saved app:

{"auth_app_ref":"slack_app","workspace_key":"work_slack"}

slack.connect is in the connection section. Open its same-origin authorization link and approve the selected scopes. Tokens are saved only in private Parameter Store fields. OAuth and auth.test must agree on the team, user ID and principal type; token prefixes are never identity evidence. Enterprise-wide installations without an exact team identity are rejected.

A slack_workspace profile represents one exact team and one principal. Bot and optional user grants are separate profiles, with their own actual scopes and rotation tokens. slack.workspaces lists safe identity and capability metadata. Use the returned workspace_ref, not the workspace display name. Omission works only for one accepted or uniquely connected profile. Several profiles require an explicit choice, even if just one has the scope for the proposed operation.

connection_status reports local grants without probing Slack. disconnect clears local tokens and scopes; it does not uninstall the app or revoke remote Slack consent. Reconnect with the same profile key to preserve identity. A changed team or principal requires a new key.

When enabled by the Slack app, expiring tokens are refreshed after the model boundary. A durable reauthorization fence is written before consuming a refresh token. Interrupted refreshes require fresh consent rather than retrying a potentially consumed token. Successful refreshes persist the replacement tokens with app/profile revision checks. Non-rotating tokens have no invented expiry. Slack token rotation.

Tools and scopes

All tool names below have the slack. prefix. The five entry tools are workspaces, connection_status, conversations, history, and thread. Discover the eight sections for additional tools.

Section Tools Actual required scopes
connection workspaces, connect, connection_status, disconnect Local lifecycle; consent requests only configured scopes
conversations.read conversations, conversation, members channels:read, groups:read, im:read, mpim:read, according to conversation kind
messages.read history, thread, message channels:history, groups:history, im:history, mpim:history, according to conversation kind
messages.write post_message, reply, update_message, delete_message chat:write
reactions reactions, add_reaction, remove_reaction reactions:read or reactions:write
files files, file_info, download_file, upload_file files:read or files:write
users users, user users:read; email is projected only with users:read.email
search search_messages User principal with search:read

A bot can optionally request chat:write.public to post to public channels where it is not a member. It is never requested automatically. Availability describes local grants; Slack still decides access to each resource. The skill never changes membership or substitutes a different principal to gain access.

Provider references verified during implementation (2026-10-01): conversations, thread scopes, posting, editing, search, presence, files.

Read and search

Conversations normalize to public_channel, private_channel, im and mpim. membership: "joined" uses the selected principal's conversations. Other listing uses accessible conversations. All listing is one bounded page; continuation handles are private, expire after 15 minutes and are bound to identity and filters. History and thread reads return at most 15 messages per call, even when a higher limit is requested. Other cursor lists return at most 100. files uses explicit bounded page numbers, with a maximum of 100 pages per query.

To summarize 50 messages, the main Agent must follow pages until it has enough messages or reaches the provider's boundary. Rate limits may require waiting. oldest and latest are exact Slack timestamp strings, preserving fractional precision. To read an exact reply, provide both its ts and its parent thread_ts. Conversation metadata may include a provider last_read; the skill does not invent unread status or mark anything read.

search_messages uses Slack's query syntax, for example from:alex after:2026-09-24 in:platform. A bot or missing search scope produces a precise failure. No channel crawl replaces unavailable search.

Text is capped at 8,000 characters per returned message. Blocks are summarized structurally (up to ten), with bounded attachments, file references and reactions. Raw event payloads, transfer URLs and file bytes are not normal JSON results. User presence is fetched only with include_presence: true. Email requires its separate grant. Provider text, profiles, links and filenames remain untrusted data.

Writes and uncertain results

Posting requires exact channel_id; replies also require parent thread_ts. Updates and deletions require exact channel_id + ts. Names and matching text cannot authorize mutation. Post/reply text is at most 4,000 characters. Optional blocks support at most ten section/divider blocks, with bounded plain-text or mrkdwn text. Arbitrary payload fields, buttons and remote images are rejected. Post/reply supports mrkdwn; update uses Slack's documented parse behavior. Link and media unfurling are disabled on new messages.

Every write uses existing native confirmation. Message deletion additionally uses the existing unsafe-action policy for external data deletion. There is no separate Slack approval dialog. Public posting receives ordinary external-write approval; this version does not infer channel size or add a public-channel threshold.

Posts/replies include an operation-stable client_msg_id. Slack's method docs mention duplicate-related errors, but do not supply a general exactly-once transport guarantee. SMTO therefore never blindly repeats a write. After a lost post response, one bounded history/thread read can recognize the exact client ID and sender. A matching text alone is never enough. Reactions use ensure-present/ensure-absent semantics; already-present/absent errors are successful no-ops. Reconciliation never interprets a truncated reaction actor list as absence.

A transport failure, uncertain provider error, malformed write response or cancellation after dispatch yields slack.mutation_outcome_unknown unless an exact read proves the desired state. Native receipts preserve effect_unknown and remote_effect_possible, preventing automatic replay. Update/delete and ambiguous file completion remain unknown for manual inspection; no second mutation is sent.

Rate limits and files

Slack 429 responses retain their Retry-After per app/workspace/method. Reads get at most three attempts. Delays up to 30 seconds are cancellable; longer delays return slack.rate_limited with the full required wait. The delay also gates later calls in the same controller process. Writes are never retried, including after known rate-limit rejection. Restarting the controller clears transient rate-limit and cursor state. Slack rate limits.

Both transfer directions are capped at 25 MiB. Upload sources must be existing conversation-owned artifact:// or artifact-workspace:// references; arbitrary host paths are rejected. Source size/hash are verified before any provider write. The current workflow is files.getUploadURLExternal, one binary upload, then files.completeUploadExternal with exact channel/thread IDs. It never invokes the retired files.upload endpoint or public-link sharing. Allocation, completion.

Downloads stream to sensitive run artifacts with sanitized filenames, measured byte bounds and size verification. URLs must be provider-returned HTTPS Slack file origins; redirects and unsupported hosts fail closed. Bearer authorization goes only to authenticated download hosts, never to external upload URLs. Incomplete transfers do not publish partial artifacts. Uncertain completion preserves the allocated file_id for inspection.

Diagnostics and limits

Canonical slack.* errors distinguish configuration, identity, scopes, membership, exact-target failures, throttling, file limits, cancellation and unknown effects, with remediation in the shared error catalog. Parameter projections always omit access/refresh tokens and client secrets, including with optional redaction off. Tool outputs scrub credential reflections. Existing content-minimization controls omit message bodies and provider content from diagnostics and portable history. OAuth callback query logs and private HTTP diagnostics are suppressed.

The implementation makes zero helper LLM calls. No administration, provisioning, retention changes, channel archive/delete, membership mutations, Socket Mode or background ingestion are included. Mandatory tests use a fake Slack provider; no live workspace validation is claimed. GovSlack and enterprise-wide grants without an exact workspace are not supported in this version.
